## Active

### D-513 — The runbook declares the suite it deploys, which is the tenant's act

> _2026-10-11 · test/blong-int-kustomize · active_

D-507 keeps the declaration out of every kustomization because which suite a namespace runs is the
tenant's decision. A runbook is that tenant for the cluster it owns, so it applies
`example/blongdeployment.yaml` after the tree instead of rendering it for somebody else to apply:
without that step the operator reconciles whatever declaration an earlier run left, which is how a
switched-off service survived a full cycle. Leaving the apply to a developer would make every green
report depend on a step outside the run. Reconsider if a runbook is ever pointed at a cluster whose
tenants are not the run.
